author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty, on the page and in the machine-readable form
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty on the request and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring letter case. A blank name filters nothing; a name nobody holds yields an empty directory, not an error.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the HTML directory is requested with it, then only those veterinarians are listed
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable directory is requested with it, then only those veterinarians are carried
given a specialty name differing from the held name only by letter case, when either form is requested with it, then it matches
given only the start of a held specialty's name, when either form is requested with it, then no veterinarian matches, because the match is on the whole name
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested with it, then the response succeeds with HTTP 200 and the veterinarian list is empty
given an empty or all-space specialty, when either form is requested with it, then every veterinarian is listed, as when no specialty is named
given no specialty on the request, when either form is requested, then both behave exactly as they do today
given a narrowed HTML directory with more matches than one page holds, when the reader follows a page link, then the next matching veterinarians are shown and the same specialty is still applied
given a narrowed HTML directory, when its page links are rendered, then each carries the specialty forward
given the machine-readable directory with no specialty named, when it is requested, then it carries every veterinarian with the specialties each holds (REQ-VET-003 baseline)
non_goals: a form field, dropdown, or any other page control for the filter — the filter is a request-address contract only in this round
filtering by veterinarian name or any attribute other than specialty; free-text veterinarian search stays out under NG-9
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: Scope covers REQ-VET-004 plus the REQ-VET-003 baseline, batched deliberately: reinstating the machine-readable directory is a status decision the code already satisfies, so on its own it would be a one-cycle slice that only makes sense alongside this filter. NG-9 is narrowed in docs/prd.md and recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-24-non-goal-veterinarian-free-text-search.md. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is not reused. Two follow-ups sit outside this agent's write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs the new ADR added to its index table, and docs/system-design.md carries a Known Defects row and a Contracts note calling the machine-readable vet route requirement-less and pending removal — both are now false and belong to system-design-expert. Three questions are recorded open in the PRD with the narrowest reading taken: a visible filter control (possible follow-up request), trimming surrounding spaces on a non-blank value (matches as supplied), and a repeated specialty value (unsupported, no behavior promised).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter lands entirely inside the vet feature package and reuses the paged-derived-query shape OwnerRepository/OwnerController already demonstrate, so no new package, layer, or dependency appears. Two things are genuinely new ground and are now recorded. First, the narrowing must happen before the page is cut, because REQ-VET-004 requires the HTML totals to count the narrowed set; that puts the match in VetRepository as a derived query rather than in the controller over a cached collection. Second, VetRepository's existing reads are cached in the 'vets' cache, which is created with neither a size limit nor eviction, so a caller-supplied specialty must not reach that cache's key space. Both decisions are in docs/adr/2026-08-24-specialty-filter-as-an-uncached-repository-query.md, and system-design.md Contracts, Threat Model, and Open Question 5 now reflect them. REQ-VET-003 needed no code: it is a status decision, and the two doc statements that contradicted it are fixed (the Known Defects row for the machine-readable route is removed, and Vets/Vet/Specialty/VetController now cite REQ-VET-003 in Implements). docs/adr/README.md gained index rows for both 2026-08-24 ADRs.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty request parameter; the model keeps its existing attributes and carries the specialty back so the page links can repeat it
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same parameter and fills the Vets wrapper from the narrowed read

VetRepository gains two specialty-matching reads mirroring its existing pair — one Pageable, one unpaged Collection — neither annotated @Cacheable; the two existing findAll methods are untouched, which is what the no-specialty acceptance criterion requires
SpecialtyFilter is the single place deciding whether a specialty is named at all, used by both routes
vets/vetList.html page links carry the specialty forward through a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter so it is URL-encoded, not appended into the literal URL string
docs/system-design.md and docs/adr/README.md are already updated by this triage; the implementer does not need to touch them for the design recorded here

patterns.description: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) — the derived paged-query-with-criterion shape the specialty query mirrors; note the vet query matches the whole name, not a prefix

controller normalizes the supplied search value and then selects the repository call — same shape here, except the blank rule lives in SpecialtyFilter rather than inline, so no new business rule enters a web controller
@DataJpaTest with an autowired VetRepository against seeded H2 — the real-datastore seam where whole-name, case-insensitive, and no-match behavior is actually observable
the project's one explicit @Query, the precedent if the derived query cannot express the match cleanly

risks.risk: Copying @Cacheable("vets") onto the new query methods puts a caller-supplied string into a cache with neither a size limit nor eviction, on an unauthenticated route.
risks.mitigation: Leave both specialty-matching methods uncached and leave the two existing findAll annotations exactly as they are. The ADR records why; system-design.md Threat Model carries the row.

risks.risk: Relying on a column collation for case-insensitivity reproduces the PostgreSQL owner-search defect on a second surface — the specialties.name column has no ignore-case typing on any vendor.
risks.mitigation: State the comparison in the query itself (IgnoreCase on the derived query) so H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL agree.

risks.risk: The join to specialties is to-many, so a vet can come back once per matching specialty row, and a derived count query over a distinct join sometimes misbehaves under paging.
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived query name; if the count query misbehaves, fall back to an explicit @Query with a matching countQuery, following PetTypeRepository as precedent. A pagination test over the narrowed list is what catches this.

risks.risk: The seeded data holds at most two vets per specialty (radiology 2, surgery 2, dentistry 1) against a page size of 5, so the 'more matches than one page holds' criterion cannot be exercised against the real datastore without changing seed data or page size.
risks.mitigation: Assert the page links carry the specialty at the web layer against a repository double returning a controlled Page, and keep the matching-semantics assertions on the @DataJpaTest seam. Do not change the seeded data to suit a test.

risks.risk: Extending the existing Mockito-stubbed VetControllerTests to cover whole-name and case-insensitive matching would assert nothing — the stub returns whatever it is told, so the test passes against a wrong query.
risks.mitigation: Matching semantics go on ClinicServiceTests (real repository, real H2). testing-principles.md asks a new test to reach for a real implementation or a hand-written double before a mock-framework stub.

risks.risk: Putting the blank-means-unfiltered rule inline in both controller methods adds a business rule to a web controller — barred by architecture-principles.md § Design Validation Checklist — and duplicates it across the two routes.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyFilter holds the rule once: immutable, equal by value, null or blank normalized at construction, unit-tested without framework context. That also moves one rule into the base of the pyramid, which testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid explicitly rewards.

notes: Scope for the implementer: SpecialtyFilter is package-private in the vet package; its exact component shape is the implementer's call, but it must be immutable, equal by value, normalize null and all-space input to the narrows-nothing case at construction, and expose both whether it narrows and the name it narrows to. Honor the PRD's three open questions as written and add no code for them: no page control, no trimming of a non-blank value (it matches as supplied, spaces included), and no handling of a repeated specialty parameter (unsupported, no behavior promised — whatever Spring's default binding does is what happens). Use the ubiquitous-language terms: Veterinarian in prose, Vet in code, Specialty, Veterinarian directory; 'specialty filter' is already the PRD's phrase for the capability, so SpecialtyFilter introduces no new vocabulary. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the ledger, so the autofix audit had nothing to judge. The two follow-ups the PRD agent flagged are closed by this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md now indexes both 2026-08-24 ADRs, and the Known Defects row plus the Contracts Implements cells calling the machine-readable route requirement-less are corrected. One incidental defect fixed along the way: the Contracts preamble claims three kinds of contract carry an em-dash in Implements while four rows did; giving Vets its REQ-VET-003 makes the claim true again.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No injection surface: matching goes through the Spring Data derived queries findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and (String, Pageable); no hand-written JPQL, no native SQL, no string concatenation into a query. The caller string is bound as a JPA parameter.

Reflected-XSS control verified at every site: grep of src/main/resources/templates/ shows ${specialty} reaches the template only inside Thymeleaf link expressions, at all five page links in vets/vetList.html (numbered loop line 30, first line 35, previous line 40, next line 46, last line 51). Each is @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}, so the value is URL-encoded as a link parameter and then attribute-escaped on output. No th:text, th:utext, inlined [[...]], or literal query-string concatenation carries the value. The prior literal-concatenation form is gone from the file.
Parameter-forgery control holds: because the value is a link-expression parameter rather than concatenated text, a value such as '&page=9' cannot terminate the parameter and append a second one.

Cache-growth decision verified in code, not just in prose: VetRepository declares @Cacheable("vets") on findAll() and findAll(Pageable) only. Both new specialty-matching reads carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) with no @Cacheable, so the caller-supplied string never becomes a cache key. CacheConfiguration still builds "vets" from a bare MutableConfiguration (no size limit, no eviction), which is exactly why the exclusion matters; no other path in the diff reintroduces the caller string as a key.

JSON surface does not echo the input: /vets returns a Vets aggregate built from repository results only. The specialty value is not reflected into the response body, so there is no JSON-context escaping question and no reflected-content vector on that route.

No information disclosure through the filter: the vet directory is public data and specialty names are already rendered on the page. A no-match request returns HTTP 200 with an empty list, which is the same response shape as a match with no holders, so the response does not distinguish an existing-but-unheld specialty from a nonexistent one in a way that discloses anything not already public.

Input normalization is safe and total: the SpecialtyFilter compact constructor collapses null, empty, and whitespace-only to null; the record is immutable and package-private, and both routes decide through it, so the blank-equals-absent rule cannot diverge between the HTML and JSON surfaces.

No secrets introduced: swept the production diff for password/secret/token/api-key/credential patterns with no hits; the change adds no configuration, no credentials, and no logging of the caller-supplied value.

Supply chain unchanged: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows no build.gradle, no version catalog, and no lockfile in the change set, so the dependency graph and its CVE exposure are identical to the reviewed basis. No new or upgraded coordinates to verify.

Unbounded parameter length was considered and is not a finding under the project's severity classification: an oversize specialty string is bound as a JPA parameter against an indexed name column, is not cached, is not reflected into HTML text, and yields an empty result. The residual concern is request-size handling already owned by the container, not new attack surface.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by one named specialty

blast_radius.note: Thirteen files but one vertical: the whole production delta is four files inside the vet feature package plus its Thymeleaf template, with no sensitive paths, no schema change, no config change, and no shared infrastructure touched; the remaining six files are PRD, system-design, ubiquitous-language and two ADRs, and three are test files.

semantic_surprise.note: The three nonobvious spots all read correctly: the derived query findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is whole-name equality ignoring case rather than a prefix, and is pinned against real H2; the page-link parameter is a Collection precisely so Thymeleaf omits it when empty rather than emitting a bare specialty=, which keeps the unnarrowed link address unchanged, and that is documented in system-design and asserted by a test; and the empty-result case cannot hit the #numbers.sequence(1, 0) descending-sequence trap because the pagination block stays behind the pre-existing totalPages > 1 guard. The template's th:each specialty variable shadows the model attribute of the same name, but only inside the table body, well outside the link block.

test_adequacy.note: The tests split along the seam that matters rather than restating the implementation: matching semantics (whole name, letter case, prefix non-match, no match, and narrowed page totals asserting totalElements is the match count and not the corpus count) sit in ClinicServiceTests against a real H2 database where the derived query actually executes, so the Mockito-stubbed controller slice never becomes the only evidence the query works; SpecialtyFilterTests exercises the blank rule with no framework at all; and the controller slice covers both routes for filtered, blank, whitespace, no-match, absent, page-links-carry-the-specialty, unfiltered-links-carry-none, and a specialty containing query-string metacharacters asserting the %26page%3D9 encoding. Each would fail against a broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: No approval carries a reservation. The single round-1 changes_requested was a concrete fixable gap (the JSON route lacked blank and no-match coverage), it was closed by adding exactly those two tests with no production change, and test-reviewer approved cleanly in round 2; the round-2 roster scoped to test-reviewer alone is the correct focused plan because the production code was untouched, so the other three round-1 approvals stand against the same code. The security reviewer explicitly reasoned about unbounded specialty length and recorded it as not a finding rather than as a lingering worry.

scope_deviation.note: The one design revision was bookkeeping, not drift: the superseding design-block says in its own words that it exists to correct the earlier record's declared paths for the path-based autofix audit and not its design, and the sole build failure was that same audit refusing two undeclared docs/adr paths. Zero build retries, zero consultations. Read against the requirement, the diff stops exactly where REQ-VET-004 stops: a URL contract with no form field, dropdown, or other page control.

rationale: Contained, well-tested, and the reviewers left nothing hanging. Read one line before you merge: the page-link parameter in VetController is a Collection, not a String, so Thymeleaf omits it when empty and an unfiltered page link stays exactly as it was. That trick is deliberate, documented, and pinned by a test.
